ranking.rationale: Best scarce-experiment choice: the only candidate directly supported by a complete training-only temporal screen with full coverage and positive movement on all four holdout dates. It is tightly scoped, low-risk, leakage-safe, and tests the entire validated feature family, though its estimated gain should be discounted modestly for feature-selection/validation-overfitting risk.

High-upside, compact affinity ablation that addresses the additive scaffold's central inability to model user-video interactions. It has no direct measured lift, so evidence is weaker than c01, but factorization machines are lower runtime and scope risk than the MLP or Deep & Cross alternatives.

A narrowly targeted interaction motivated by the positive request-context result. It is materially more specific and lower-risk than broad cross architectures, but sparse video-tab cells and hash collisions reduce confidence, and it partially duplicates the context hypothesis already best tested by c01.

Low-runtime personalized-affinity test with a reasonable inductive bias and no new features. It is largely duplicative of c05, has weaker expressive capacity due to normalization, and lacks direct empirical support, so it should follow the factorization-machine test.

Potentially captures useful ID-context interactions, but combines architecture replacement with all context fields, making attribution weak and scope excessive for one scarce experiment. It also risks overfitting rare ID-context conjunctions and is partially subsumed by c01 plus c05.

Clean, inexpensive objective-alignment test with no feature leakage or architectural confounding. However, its benefit is speculative, its target alignment is imperfect because official GAUC is positive-count weighted rather than equal-user weighted, and it may harm nDCG@5.

A focused user-time interaction is plausible from the context screen and remains low runtime risk. Evidence is indirect, sparse user-hour cells create generalization risk, and it duplicates both the broader context hypothesis and interaction-model candidates.

A viable personalized-affinity model, but it is substantially duplicative of c05 and c10 while adding MLP capacity, tuning sensitivity, and medium runtime risk. There is no evidence that its extra nonlinear flexibility is needed over a simpler interaction model.

Low-risk diagnostic ablation, but testing tab alone sacrifices the strongest available evidence, which supports the combined context family rather than an individual field. It is also dominated operationally by c01 for a single experiment.
Similarly safe and interpretable, but has only family-level evidence and a low expected standalone gain. It is dominated by c01 and less directly motivated than the tab interaction candidate.

Metric direction is appealing, but pair sampling, training-user label composition, and objective tuning create meaningful validation-overfitting and runtime risk. The stated medium leakage risk and uncertain nDCG@5 tradeoff make it unsuitable for the sole experiment.

Lowest expected gain and confidence among the candidates. Weekday is coarse, only indirectly supported by the grouped screen, and the isolated test is dominated by the complete low-risk context ablation in c01.
